definitions.gloss: inn waitress, ryokan attendant, traditional restaurant server
definitions.explanation: A female attendant at a traditional Japanese inn (ryokan) or traditional restaurant (ryoutei) who serves food, prepares rooms, and attends to guests. Typically wears a kimono.

examples.japanese: {仲居|なかい}さんが{部屋|へや}に{案内|あんない}してくれた。
examples.english: The inn attendant showed us to our room.

examples.japanese: {仲居|なかい}さんが{着物|きもの}を{着|き}て{食事|しょくじ}を{運|はこ}んできた。
examples.english: The inn attendant brought the meal wearing a kimono.

examples.japanese: {老舗|しにせ}{旅館|りょかん}の{仲居|なかい}さんはおもてなしの{心|こころ}が{行|ゆ}き{届|とど}いていて、{滞在|たいざい}がとても{快適|かいてき}だった。
examples.english: The attendants at the long-established ryokan had thorough hospitality, making the stay very comfortable.

notes:
Traditionally a female role. Usually addressed as {仲居|なかい}さん with the honorific さん. The role is closely associated with Japanese hospitality culture (おもてなし).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{仲居|なかい}さん (inn attendant — with honorific)
・{仲居|なかい}として{働|はたら}く (to work as an inn attendant)
・{旅館|りょかん}の{仲居|なかい} (ryokan attendant)
・{料亭|りょうてい}の{仲居|なかい} (traditional restaurant attendant)

CULTURAL NOTES:
At a {旅館|りょかん}, the {仲居|なかい} typically welcomes guests, serves tea, explains the room and facilities, brings meals to the guest room, and lays out the {布団|ふとん} (futon bedding). The role is a central part of the traditional Japanese inn experience.
